body.statement:
Suppose that \(p_n=p\) is fixed before \(n\to\infty\).  Define
\[
 \mu_\gamma=\mathbb E\!\left[Z\{\sigma(\gamma Z)-1/2\}\right]
 =\gamma v_\gamma,
 \qquad
 I_\gamma=\mathbb E\!\left[Z^2\sigma'(\gamma Z)\right],
\]
let \(e_1\) be the first coordinate vector in \(\mathbb R^p\), and set
\[
 \Sigma_T=\frac18 I_p,
 \qquad
 \Sigma_E=\frac1{16}I_p-\frac14\mu_\gamma^2e_1e_1^\top,
 \qquad
 \Sigma_D=\frac14\operatorname{diag}(I_\gamma,v_\gamma,\ldots,v_\gamma).
\]
For each \(j\in\mathcal J\), the globally selected estimator satisfies
\[
 \widehat\beta_{jn}\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt n\,\widehat\beta_{jn}\Rightarrow
 \mathcal N_p\!\left(0,\frac{16}{\lambda^2}\Sigma_j\right).
\]
If \(Z_j\sim\mathcal N_p(0,\Sigma_j)\), then
\[
 n\mathcal R_{jn}\Rightarrow \frac2\lambda Z_j^\top Z_j.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \Sigma_D\prec\Sigma_E\prec\Sigma_T.
\]
In particular, the signal-coordinate gap has the exact identity
\[
 (\Sigma_E-\Sigma_D)_{11}
 =\frac14\operatorname{Var}\!\left[Z\{\sigma(\gamma Z)-1/2\}\right]>0.
\]
Finally, \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n)\to1\) in this fixed-dimensional regime, so the method-\(E\) conclusion concerns the unique exact-balancing weights with probability tending to one and uses no entropy-balancing property of the complement-event default.
body.justification: The repaired theorem supplies a complete fixed-dimensional global estimator and regret limit law without conditioning on the open proportional system.
body.gap: Exact same-coordinate linear balance has covariance strictly between true-propensity IPW and oracle DR; proportional small-aspect constants require a separate boundary-uniform theorem.
body.consumer: The result is a low-dimensional calibration and a warning that exact linear balance is not automatic oracle efficiency.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\) and let \(G_{jn}=\nabla F_{jn}(0)\).  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}dimensional\mbox{-}joint\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}covariances}\),
\[
 \sqrt n\,G_{jn}\Rightarrow Z_j,
 \qquad Z_j\sim\mathcal N_p(0,\Sigma_j),
 \tag{1}
\]
and the certified exact-balance and rank event has probability tending to one.  We first justify that the lexicographically selected global maximizer, rather than merely a stationary root, is localized at zero.

For methods \(T\) and \(D\), the reward part of \(F_{jn}\) has population mean zero: randomization gives \(\mathbb E(SY\mid q)=0\), while the outcome model gives \(\mathbb E\{S(Y-m)\mid q,A\}=0\).  For method \(E\), fixed-dimensional balance feasibility and the entropy-score expansion in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}dimensional\mbox{-}joint\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}covariances}\) give \(\eta_{an}=O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\).  Hence, uniformly over the compact ball \(\mathcal B_n\), each tilted arm mean of
\[
 Y\{\sigma(q^\top\beta)-1/2\}
\]
converges to its common population mean, and their difference converges to zero.  To see the required uniformity directly, take a finite \(\delta\)-net of the fixed-dimensional compact ball.  At the net points the ordinary law of large numbers applies; between net points, the mean-value bound
\[
 |\sigma(q^\top\beta)-\sigma(q^\top\widetilde\beta)|
 \le \frac14\|q\|_2\|\beta-\widetilde\beta\|_2
\]
and \(\mathbb E\|q\|_2<\infty\) control the interpolation.  The same argument applies after multiplication by \(\exp(q^\top\eta_{an})\), because \(\eta_{an}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and Gaussian exponential moments are finite in a fixed neighborhood of zero.  Applying the same finite-net argument to \(h(q^\top\beta)\) yields
\[
 \sup_{\beta\in\mathcal B_n}
 \left|F_{jn}(\beta)+\lambda g(\|\beta\|_2)\right|
 \longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}radial\mbox{-}invariance}\) gives \(g(0)=0\) and \(g(r)>0\) for every \(r>0\).  Therefore the limit in (2) has the unique maximizer zero.  For any \(\varepsilon\in(0,R)\), continuity and strict positivity give
\[
 \inf_{\varepsilon\le r\le R}\lambda g(r)>0.
\]
Together with (2), this implies
\[
 \widehat\beta_{jn}\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}0.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus the radius constraint is inactive with probability tending to one, because \(R>0\).

Direct differentiation of the definitions gives
\[
 \sigma'(0)=\frac14,
 \qquad \sigma''(0)=0,
 \qquad h'(z)=z\sigma'(z),
 \qquad h''(0)=\frac14.
\]
Consequently, for every sample and every method,
\[
 \nabla^2F_{jn}(0)
 =-\frac\lambda4\frac{Q_n^\top Q_n}{n}.
 \tag{4}
\]
For fixed \(p\), coordinatewise second-moment laws and a finite union bound give
\[
 \frac{Q_n^\top Q_n}{n}\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}I_p.
 \tag{5}
\]
The finite-net argument used in (2), now with the integrable Gaussian envelope for the second derivatives, also gives local stochastic equicontinuity of \(\nabla^2F_{jn}\) at zero.  For method \(E\), the same conclusion follows because \(\eta_{an}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and the corresponding exponential envelopes have finite Gaussian moments.  Hence (3)--(5) imply
\[
 \int_0^1\nabla^2F_{jn}(t\widehat\beta_{jn})\,dt
 \longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}-\frac\lambda4 I_p.
 \tag{6}
\]
The limiting matrix is invertible because \(\lambda>0\).

On the event that the selected maximizer is interior, its gradient is zero.  The fundamental theorem of calculus, (6), and (1) therefore yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0
 &=G_{jn}+\left\{\int_0^1\nabla^2F_{jn}
       (t\widehat\beta_{jn})\,dt\right\}\widehat\beta_{jn},\\
 \sqrt n\,\widehat\beta_{jn}
 &=\frac4\lambda\sqrt n\,G_{jn}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \Rightarrow \frac4\lambda Z_j.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
This proves the asserted centered normal limit.

It remains to transform estimation error into causal regret.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}radial\mbox{-}invariance}\) gives
\[
 g'(r)=r\,\mathbb E[Z^2\sigma'(rZ)].
\]
Since \(0<\sigma'(x)\le1/4\), dominated convergence gives \(g'(r)/r\to1/4\) as \(r\downarrow0\).  Integration from zero to \(r\) shows
\[
 g(r)=\frac{r^2}{8}+o(r^2).
 \tag{8}
\]
Combining (3), (7), (8), and the exact regret identity gives
\[
 n\mathcal R_{jn}
 =n\lambda g(\|\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2)
 =\frac\lambda8\|\sqrt n\,\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2^2+o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \Rightarrow \frac2\lambda Z_j^\top Z_j.
\]
Finally, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}dimensional\mbox{-}joint\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}covariances}\) proves \(\Sigma_D\prec\Sigma_E\prec\Sigma_T\), including the displayed signal-coordinate identity.  No proportional limit, interchange of limits, or conclusion from the open joint system has been used.
